row.basis: teach the divine paths
row.note: The commentary treats guidance as both knowing a route and being led along it; the psalm asks God to make his ways known and teach his paths.

row.basis: lead me in your truth
row.note: The commentary's “lead us on the straight path” is a prayer for continuing direction; this verse asks God to lead the speaker in truth and teach him.

row.basis: teach me your way; unite my heart
row.note: The commentary links walking God's way with exclusive worship; this prayer asks to be taught God's way in order to walk in truth with an undivided heart.

row.basis: good Spirit; level ground
row.note: The commentary asks God to guide a dependent traveler and stresses a level, sustained walk; the psalm asks God to teach his will and have his good Spirit lead the speaker on level ground.

row.basis: level path amid enemies
row.note: The commentary hears the straight path as a route that must be followed and protected; the psalm asks God to teach his way and lead the speaker on a level path despite hostile witnesses.

row.basis: paths of righteousness
row.note: The commentary asks for guidance along a lived route; the psalm's shepherd leads the speaker on tracks of righteousness, joining direction with sustained care.

row.basis: supplication; straight path; brooks
row.note: The commentary's collective petition asks God to keep worshipers on the way; Jeremiah pictures a weeping returning people led by God, with supplication, along a straight path to water where they will not stumble.

row.basis: blind led on an unknown way
row.note: The commentary describes people who cannot find the route without a guide; God promises here to lead the blind by a way they do not know, turning darkness to light and rough ground level.

row.basis: the voice says, “this is the way”
row.note: The commentary presents guidance as an ongoing walk rather than a one-time conversion; this verse gives travelers a voice directing them to keep walking the way when they veer right or left.

row.basis: God makes paths straight
row.note: The commentary asks God to lead a community already devoted to him; Proverbs says that acknowledging God in all one's ways brings his making the paths straight.

row.basis: teaches; leads in the way
row.note: The commentary makes God the source of guidance and its ongoing teacher; here God says he teaches what is beneficial and leads Israel in the way it should go.

row.basis: the path of the righteous made level
row.note: The commentary connects the straight path with an even, unbent course; Isaiah says the path of the righteous is level because God makes it smooth.

row.basis: highway of holiness; the redeemed
row.note: The commentary identifies the requested route with the company of those favored by God; Isaiah's highway is called the holy way and is reserved for the redeemed returning to Zion.

row.basis: straight road to an inhabited city
row.note: The commentary says the road ends in a home that receives the traveler; after the lost and hungry wanderers cry for help, God leads them by a straight way to a city where they can dwell.

row.basis: travelers cry to God for help
row.note: The commentary connects the request to be guided with the preceding plea for help; this verse depicts travelers crying to God in distress and being delivered before the straight road and city of the next verse.

row.basis: God leads the redeemed to his holy abode
row.note: The commentary's journey ends in a place of welcome; the Song of the Sea says God leads the people he redeemed toward his holy dwelling by steadfast love.

row.basis: bring and plant at the sanctuary
row.note: The commentary hears guidance as arrival at a home or refuge; Moses' song asks God to bring the people to his mountain and plant them at the sanctuary he established.

row.basis: the Lord goes before Israel
row.note: The commentary names Moses and Aaron as people led on the straight way; in the Exodus narrative God goes before Israel as cloud and fire to guide their day-and-night wilderness journey.

row.basis: God goes ahead to find a camp
row.note: The commentary's guide goes in front and shows where to walk; Moses recalls God going ahead of Israel to find camping places and show the route.

row.basis: the Lord alone guided Israel
row.note: The commentary says the request is directed only to the one who can truly guide; Moses' song says the Lord alone led Jacob, with no foreign god beside him.

row.basis: the ark goes before, seeking a resting place
row.note: The commentary's guide goes ahead of the travelers and leads toward a place of rest; the ark precedes Israel in the wilderness to seek a resting place for them.

row.basis: the guide leads to springs
row.note: The commentary connects guidance with reaching a place of shelter and sustaining water; Isaiah says the compassionate guide leads the returning people to springs of water.

row.basis: continual guidance like a watered garden
row.note: The commentary insists that guidance continues along the road and mentions water that sustains life; Isaiah promises that God will guide continually and make the people like a watered garden.

row.basis: the highways to Zion in the heart
row.note: The commentary's path is walked toward a welcomed destination; the pilgrim psalm blesses those whose hearts are set on the highways to God's house.

row.basis: the valley becomes springs
row.note: The commentary associates the road with sustaining water and support for the traveler; this pilgrimage verse describes a dry valley becoming a place of springs on the way to Zion.

row.basis: from strength to strength, appearing before God
row.note: The commentary says the route is a walk that continues until arrival; the pilgrim psalm describes travelers gaining strength as they go until each appears before God in Zion.

row.basis: make a level path for your feet
row.note: The commentary develops uprightness as a bodily walk that must remain straight; Proverbs tells the hearer to make a level path for the feet and have all ways be firm.

row.basis: do not swerve right or left
row.note: The commentary places the straight path between deviations and asks for help to stay on it; Proverbs commands the traveler not to turn right or left but to keep the foot from evil.

row.basis: ask for the good ancient way and walk in it
row.note: The commentary treats guidance as something to be requested repeatedly and then walked; Jeremiah tells the people to ask for the ancient paths, find the good way, and walk in it, though they refuse.

row.basis: the Lord knows the righteous way; the wicked way perishes
row.note: The commentary distinguishes the favored people's path from ways that end in loss; Psalm 1 contrasts the way of the righteous, known by the Lord, with the way of the wicked, which perishes.

row.basis: choose life rather than death
row.note: The commentary names a straight path between opposed outcomes; Moses sets life and death before Israel and calls them to choose life by loving and obeying God.

row.basis: the Lord's way is justice and righteousness
row.note: The commentary says the path is a lived course shaped by worship; God says Abraham's household is to keep the Lord's way by doing righteousness and justice.

row.basis: limping between two allegiances
row.note: The commentary depicts the traveler as wavering and asks for an unwavering path; Elijah challenges Israel for limping between the Lord and Baal and demands a clear choice of whom to serve.

row.basis: the right way leads to a bride's home
row.note: The commentary develops guidance as escorting a bride to the home where she will be received; Abraham's servant says the Lord led him on the right way to find Rebekah as a wife for Isaac.

row.basis: offerings brought to the chosen place
row.note: The commentary's h-d-y word family includes an offering animal brought to its appointed sanctuary; Deuteronomy directs Israel to bring sacrifices and firstborn offerings to the place God chooses.

row.basis: trust; help; make your ways straight
row.note: The commentary presents the request for guidance as trustful dependence on God, not self-direction; Sirach tells the faithful to trust God for help, make their ways straight, and hope in him.

row.basis: ask God to make your ways straight
row.note: The commentary frames guidance as a direct request to God along life's journey; Tobit advises blessing God and asking him to make one's ways and plans straight.

row.basis: paths set right by divine wisdom
row.note: The commentary asks God to lead a community into the right way; Wisdom says that by divine wisdom the paths of people on earth were set right and they learned what pleases God.

row.basis: Tefillat ha-derekh
row.note: The commentary's petition asks God to lead the worshipers along the way; the travelers' prayer asks God to lead and direct the traveler safely on the road.

row.basis: prayers on entering and leaving a city
row.note: The commentary hears guidance as a journey toward a place that will receive the traveler; this passage gives prayers asking God to lead a traveler into and out of a city in peace.

row.basis: the two spirits and their ways
row.note: The commentary places the straight way between the ways of those favored and those who go astray; the Community Rule develops a moral choice between the paths of truth and perversity, light and darkness.

row.basis: the straight path a person should choose
row.note: The commentary asks God to lead a worshiping community on the straight way; this rabbinic teaching asks which straight path a person should choose and defines it by ethical conduct and its effects on others.

row.basis: the perilous afterlife path between fire and water
row.note: The commentary explicitly corrects the popular image of ṣirāṭ as an afterlife bridge, saying the Qur'anic word is a road walked in this life; 4 Ezra pictures the narrow, dangerous path to the future city between fire and deep water.

row.basis: two ways, life and death
row.note: The commentary names the straight way against the ways of anger and straying; the Didache opens its moral instruction by setting the way of life against the way of death.

row.basis: honest weights and balances
row.note: The commentary hears mustaqīm's straightness as a scale that does not tip to either side; Leviticus commands honest weights and measures, making uprightness a practice of fair judgment.

row.basis: false balances are rejected
row.note: The commentary links straightness with keeping the balance from leaning; Proverbs says dishonest scales are an abomination to the Lord, while a just weight pleases him.

row.basis: the scales belong to the Lord
row.note: The commentary treats balance as part of the requested upright path; Proverbs says accurate scales and weights belong to the Lord, grounding fair measure in divine order.

row.basis: Arabic q-w-m; Hebrew q-w-m in “walk upright”
row.note: The commentary labels al-mustaqīm with Arabic root q-w-m and develops upright bodily walking; Leviticus uses the cognate Hebrew root in saying God made Israel walk erect after breaking the yoke.

row.basis: Arabic q-w-m; Hebrew q-w-m, rise and stand
row.note: The commentary labels al-mustaqīm with Arabic q-w-m and associates it with an upright walk; this verse uses the cognate Hebrew root for rising and standing upright, in contrast to enemies who fall.

row.basis: God upholds the falling and raises the bowed
row.note: The commentary describes a traveler who sways and needs support before walking steadily; the psalm says God supports those who are falling and raises those bowed down.

row.basis: the Lord holds the hand of one who falls
row.note: The commentary's route includes a dependent walker who needs support to continue; the psalm says even if the righteous person falls, the Lord holds his hand.

row.basis: humans cannot direct their own steps
row.note: The commentary asks God to guide the collective because the traveler needs an outside guide; Jeremiah says a person's way is not in his own control and he cannot direct his steps.

row.basis: a way that seems right ends in death
row.note: The commentary warns that a path's goodness depends on where it leads and who walks it; Proverbs warns that a way may seem right yet end in death.

row.basis: guide our feet into the way of peace
row.note: The commentary asks for guidance on a path that leads to a welcomed end; Zechariah's hymn says God's mercy will guide “our feet” into the way of peace, from darkness toward light.

row.basis: “lead us not into temptation”
row.note: The commentary notes a communal “us” speaking directly to God in a pleading imperative; the Lord's Prayer likewise addresses God as “you” and asks collectively not to be led into trial but to be delivered from evil.

row.basis: belief that still asks for help
row.note: The commentary says people already on the way still ask to be guided at every step; the father who says “I believe” immediately asks Jesus to help his unbelief.

row.basis: the shepherd goes ahead and the sheep follow
row.note: The commentary hears the guide as a leader who walks in front so others can follow; Jesus' shepherd calls his own sheep and goes ahead of them, and they follow.

row.basis: the Spirit guides into truth
row.note: The commentary reserves guidance to God and connects the path with truth; Jesus says the Spirit of truth will guide the disciples into all truth.

row.basis: “unless someone guides me”
row.note: The commentary describes a traveler unable to find the route alone; the Ethiopian reader asks how he can understand Isaiah unless someone guides him, and Philip joins him as an interpreter.

row.basis: the Christian movement called “the Way”
row.note: The commentary stresses a path that is walked and followed, not a one-time threshold; Acts calls the community Saul seeks to arrest “the Way,” naming the movement as a lived route.

row.basis: the way that leads to life
row.note: The commentary distinguishes the straight way from roads ending in loss; Jesus describes a narrow way leading to life, found by few, against the broad way leading to destruction.

row.basis: the Father's house as destination
row.note: The commentary hears the road as leading to a home where the traveler is received; Jesus speaks of many dwelling places in his Father's house and going to prepare a place for his followers.

row.basis: Jesus as the way to the Father
row.note: The commentary asks God to guide the collective on God's straight path; John identifies Jesus himself as the way through whom people come to the Father, giving the shared journey-to-God image a distinct Christian mediation.

row.basis: a new and living way into the sanctuary
row.note: The commentary's path leads to a place of divine welcome; Hebrews describes access to the holy place through a new and living way opened through the veil, identified with Jesus' flesh.

row.basis: straight paths for the feet; healing the lame
row.note: The commentary develops upright walking and the support needed by a wavering traveler; Hebrews applies the “straight paths” image to a community so the lame may be healed rather than disabled.

row.basis: abandoning the straight way
row.note: The commentary says guidance must be sought again because a person can leave the path after finding it; Peter describes false teachers who have left the straight way and gone astray.

row.basis: grace as a gift, not earned payment
row.note: The commentary says the requested guidance is a loving gift rather than a wage; Ephesians says salvation is by grace as God's gift, not the result of works.

row.basis: good works prepared for walking
row.note: The commentary joins the gift of guidance to a path that must actually be walked; Ephesians says God prepared good works beforehand for people to walk in.

row.basis: the Lamb shepherds to springs of water
row.note: The commentary combines a leading guide with the road's life-giving destination; Revelation says the Lamb will shepherd the multitude and guide them to springs of living water.

row.basis: following in the leader's steps
row.note: The commentary pictures guidance as following an advance leader; Peter says Christ left an example so believers may follow in his steps.

row.basis: John applies Isaiah's straight-way prophecy to his own mission
row.note: The commentary hears a requested path as the route along which a community must walk; John the Baptist identifies himself as the wilderness voice of Isaiah 40:3, interpreting preparation of the Lord's way as his prophetic task.

row.basis: lead and guide for your name's sake
row.note: The commentary asks God to guide the worshipers along the way; this psalm asks God, as refuge, to lead and guide the speaker for his name's sake.

row.basis: instruction and counsel on the way
row.note: The commentary presents guidance as ongoing accompaniment; God promises here to instruct and teach the way, keeping watch and giving counsel.

row.basis: light and truth lead to the holy hill
row.note: The commentary's route ends in God's welcoming presence; the psalm asks God to send light and truth to lead the speaker to the holy mountain and dwelling.

row.basis: our guide forever
row.note: The commentary's “us” asks God for guidance as a community; this psalm says of God, “this is our God,” who guides us forever.

row.basis: make me walk the path of your commands
row.note: The commentary asks for a route that is actually walked; this prayer asks God to make the speaker walk the path of the commandments and says that he delights in it.

row.basis: a lamp to the feet and light to the path
row.note: The commentary develops guidance through signs and landmarks; the psalm calls God's word a lamp for the feet and a light on the path.

row.basis: make my steps firm; do not let sin rule
row.note: The commentary asks for continuing guidance and protection from leaving the way; this prayer asks God to make the speaker's steps firm and keep wrongdoing from ruling him.

row.basis: feet set on rock; steps made firm
row.note: The commentary's traveler needs support to move steadily after losing the way; the psalm describes being lifted from a pit, set on rock, and given firm steps.

row.basis: God led Israel like a flock
row.note: The commentary develops the guide who goes ahead of dependent travelers; this poetic retelling says God led Israel safely like a flock through the wilderness.

row.basis: God guards the paths of justice
row.note: The commentary joins the straight path to just balance and right conduct; Proverbs says God guards the paths of justice and preserves the way of his faithful ones.

row.basis: the righteous path brightens as daybreak
row.note: The commentary stresses that guidance is a continuing walk, not a single arrival; Proverbs pictures the righteous path growing brighter until full day.

row.basis: God directs the steps
row.note: The commentary says even worshipers already on the way need God to lead them at each step; Proverbs distinguishes a person's plans from the Lord's direction of the steps.

row.basis: road markers for the returning traveler
row.note: The commentary develops signs and landmarks that help a traveler find the route; Jeremiah tells the returning people to set up road markers and guideposts and remember the highway they traveled.

row.basis: God chooses a protective detour
row.note: The commentary's “straight path” is a divinely chosen route, not merely the shortest line; God deliberately does not lead Israel by the Philistine road because seeing war might make them return to Egypt.

row.basis: the detour protects Israel from turning back
row.note: The commentary treats guidance as God's care for travelers; the Mekhilta reads the longer Exodus route as protective pedagogy, since the newly freed people might turn back when faced with war.

row.basis: a messenger goes ahead and brings Israel to the prepared place
row.note: The commentary's guide leads from the front and brings travelers to their destination; God promises to send a messenger ahead of Israel to guard them and bring them to the prepared place.

row.basis: prepare a straight highway for God
row.note: The commentary hears a path that must be made straight and walked; Isaiah calls for a straight highway in the wilderness as the Lord comes to his people.

row.basis: the shepherd gathers lambs and gently leads
row.note: The commentary describes both a guide who goes ahead and a dependent traveler who needs support; Isaiah pictures God carrying lambs close and gently leading the nursing sheep.

row.basis: God teaches Ephraim to walk and takes him by the arms
row.note: The commentary portrays a traveler who sways and needs support; God recalls teaching Ephraim to walk and taking him by the arms, though Ephraim did not recognize the healing.

row.basis: leading with cords of kindness
row.note: The commentary connects guidance with gentle, loving care rather than payment; Hosea describes God leading Israel with human kindness and cords of love.

row.basis: God shepherds and gives the flock rest
row.note: The commentary asks for a guide who leads dependent travelers to a place of welcome; God promises to shepherd his own flock and make them lie down in safety.

row.basis: wilderness turned into pools and dry ground into springs
row.note: The commentary connects the route with sustaining water and the land's life-giving support; this verse pictures God transforming the wilderness into pools and dry ground into springs.

row.basis: a blind guide and a blind follower both fall
row.note: The commentary says a guide who cannot see the route cannot lead others; Jesus asks whether a blind person can guide another blind person without both falling into a pit.

row.basis: the Father draws people to the Son
row.note: The commentary insists that ultimate guidance belongs to God; Jesus says no one can come to him unless the Father draws that person.

row.basis: walk in the light before darkness overtakes you
row.note: The commentary warns that the traveler can lose the way after having found it; Jesus tells his hearers to walk while they have the light, lest darkness overtake them and leave them unable to know where they are going.

row.basis: God makes a way out of temptation
row.note: The commentary pictures an ambush on the straight path and asks for continued guidance; Paul says God will not let testing exceed what can be borne and will provide a way of escape.

row.basis: a generation that strays in heart and does not know God's ways
row.note: The commentary says guidance must be renewed because people can turn aside after being led; Hebrews recalls the wilderness generation as continually straying in heart and not knowing God's ways.

row.basis: those led by God's Spirit are God's children
row.note: The commentary makes divine guidance the continuing mark of those who worship God; Paul identifies those led by God's Spirit as children of God.

row.basis: two ways, light and darkness, under opposed powers
row.note: The commentary sets the straight path against straying and describes an adversary lying in wait on it; Barnabas develops two moral ways, light and darkness, under God's angels and Satan's angels.
